note: Community question bank for AWS Study Hub. Each question: id, cert, domain, question, options[], answer (index into options), explanation. Contributions welcome via PR.

questions.question: A company needs to run a workload that can be interrupted and restarted without data loss, and it must complete within 24 hours. Which EC2 pricing option provides the MOST cost savings?
questions.explanation: Spot Instances offer up to 90% off On-Demand. Because the workload tolerates interruption and has a flexible 24-hour window, Spot is ideal. Reserved requires a 1-3 year commitment, and Dedicated Hosts are the most expensive.

questions.question: Under the AWS Shared Responsibility Model, which task is the CUSTOMER's responsibility when using Amazon RDS?
options: Configuring security groups and network access
questions.explanation: For managed services like RDS, AWS handles OS/engine patching and hardware. The customer configures security groups, NACLs, IAM, encryption settings, backups, and owns the data.

questions.question: Which AWS pricing model lets you commit to a consistent amount of compute usage (measured in $/hour) for a 1- or 3-year term in exchange for lower prices?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans give discounted rates in return for a committed spend ($/hour) over 1 or 3 years, and are more flexible than standard Reserved Instances.

questions.question: A startup wants to avoid large upfront hardware purchases and pay only for the compute it uses. Which cloud benefit does this describe?
options: Trading capital expense for variable expense
questions.explanation: Paying only for what you consume, instead of buying hardware upfront, is the classic 'trade capital expense (CapEx) for variable expense (OpEx)' benefit of cloud computing.

questions.question: Which AWS Support plan is the MINIMUM required to get a response time of less than 1 hour for production-down cases and a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM)?
questions.explanation: A dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM) is included with Enterprise Support. Business Support offers fast response times but no TAM; Developer and Basic do not offer production-critical response times.

questions.question: Which AWS service helps you centrally manage billing and apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) across multiple AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing and lets you apply SCPs to accounts/OUs. Control Tower builds a landing zone on top of it, but the core account and SCP management is Organizations.

questions.question: A company wants a fully managed relational database and does not want to manage servers or patching. Which service should they choose?
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, etc.) that handles patching, backups, and failover. DynamoDB is NoSQL, Redshift is a data warehouse, and self-managed EC2 requires you to run everything.

questions.question: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on the ability of a workload to recover from failures and meet demand?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar covers a workload's ability to recover from failures, scale to meet demand, and mitigate disruptions. There are six pillars in total.

questions.question: Which service delivers content to users with low latency by caching it at edge locations around the world?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is the CDN that caches content at edge locations for low-latency delivery. Route 53 is DNS, and Global Accelerator improves availability/performance for TCP/UDP but is not a CDN cache.

questions.question: Which tool provides cost visualization and lets you forecast future AWS spend based on historical usage?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer visualizes and forecasts spend from historical data. AWS Budgets sets thresholds/alerts, the Pricing Calculator estimates future architectures, and Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.

questions.question: A web application has high read traffic on its MySQL database. The team wants to improve read performance WITHOUT changing application code. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
questions.explanation: Read Replicas offload reads and need no app changes if handled at the connection layer. ElastiCache requires code to check the cache first, Multi-AZ is for HA (standby is not readable), and Aurora migration is more effort.

questions.question: A company wants S3 objects accessible ONLY through CloudFront and never directly via the S3 URL. What should they configure?
options: Set the S3 bucket ACL to private
questions.explanation: OAC restricts the S3 bucket so only the CloudFront service principal can read it (enforced via bucket policy). Signed URLs control who can access CloudFront content, not how CloudFront reaches S3.

questions.question: An application must remain available even if an entire Availability Zone fails. Which approach BEST meets this requirement?
options: Deploy a larger EC2 instance type
Deploy across multiple AZs behind an Elastic Load Balancer
Use an S3 Gateway VPC endpoint
questions.explanation: Spreading instances across multiple AZs behind an ELB provides fault tolerance: if one AZ fails, traffic routes to healthy instances in other AZs. Instance size alone does not add resilience.

questions.question: Objects in an S3 bucket are rarely accessed after 30 days but must be retrievable within milliseconds when needed. Which storage class is MOST cost-effective?
questions.explanation: S3 Standard-IA is for infrequently accessed data that still needs millisecond retrieval, at lower storage cost than Standard. Glacier has retrieval delays, and One Zone-IA sacrifices multi-AZ durability.

questions.question: A queue-based system must ensure messages are processed exactly once and in the exact order they were sent. Which service configuration is appropriate?
questions.explanation: SQS FIFO queues guarantee ordering and exactly-once processing. SQS Standard offers best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery. SNS is pub/sub, and Firehose is streaming delivery, not ordered queue processing.

questions.question: EC2 instances in a private subnet need to download OS patches from the internet but must not be reachable from the internet. What should be used?
options: Internet Gateway attached to the private subnet
NAT Gateway in a public subnet
questions.explanation: A NAT Gateway in a public subnet lets private instances make outbound-only connections to the internet. An Internet Gateway would make them reachable, and Egress-Only IGW is for IPv6 only.

questions.question: An application needs single-digit millisecond latency at massive scale for a key-value workload with unpredictable traffic spikes. Which database is the BEST fit?
questions.explanation: DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, and on-demand capacity absorbs unpredictable spikes without capacity planning. Redshift is analytics, and RDS/Aurora are relational.

questions.question: A stateless web tier sees predictable baseline load plus occasional spikes. Which purchasing mix is MOST cost-effective while handling spikes?
options: Reserved/Savings Plans for baseline plus On-Demand or Spot for spikes
All Reserved Instances sized for peak
questions.explanation: Cover the steady baseline with Reserved Instances or Savings Plans (lowest rate for known usage), and handle variable spikes with On-Demand or Spot. Sizing all-Reserved for peak wastes money off-peak.

questions.question: A company wants to give an application on EC2 permission to read from an S3 bucket without storing long-term credentials on the instance. What is the recommended approach?
options: Store IAM user access keys in the app config
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
Use the root account access keys
questions.explanation: An IAM role attached to the instance provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials via the instance metadata service, with no long-term keys to manage or leak.

questions.question: Which combination provides a decoupled, scalable architecture for processing uploaded files asynchronously?
options: EC2 polling S3 directly on a loop
S3 event notification to SQS, consumed by an Auto Scaling worker fleet
Synchronous API Gateway to a single EC2 instance
questions.explanation: S3 event notifications to an SQS queue, consumed by workers that scale on queue depth, decouples producers from consumers and scales with load, a core resilient/scalable pattern.

questions.question: A Lambda function's IAM role grants s3:GetObject, but calls fail with AccessDenied on a bucket whose bucket policy has an explicit Deny for all principals. Why?
options: The IAM role needs s3:ListBucket too
An explicit Deny always overrides any Allow
Lambda cannot access S3 without a VPC endpoint
The role trust policy is misconfigured
questions.explanation: In IAM policy evaluation, an explicit Deny always wins over any Allow. The bucket policy must be changed to remove the Deny or add an exception for the Lambda execution role ARN.

questions.question: Which Lambda invocation type is used when Amazon S3 triggers a function on object upload?
questions.explanation: S3 invokes Lambda asynchronously: the event is queued, Lambda retries twice on failure, and a Dead Letter Queue or destination can capture failures. API Gateway is synchronous; SQS/Kinesis/DynamoDB Streams are poll-based.

questions.question: A team wants to shift 10% of traffic to a new Lambda version, monitor it, then shift the rest. Which deployment approach does this describe?
questions.explanation: A canary deployment routes a small percentage (e.g., 10%) to the new version for a period, then shifts the remainder once it looks healthy. CodeDeploy supports canary and linear traffic shifting for Lambda aliases.

questions.question: A developer needs to store a database password securely with automatic rotation and native RDS integration. Which service is the BEST fit?
options: Environment variables in the Lambda function
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager provides built-in automatic rotation via Lambda and native integration with RDS/Redshift. Parameter Store Standard has no built-in rotation, and env vars/S3 are not purpose-built secret stores with rotation.

questions.question: A DynamoDB query returns a LastEvaluatedKey in the response. What does this indicate?
options: The query failed and must be retried
There are more results; use it as ExclusiveStartKey to paginate
questions.explanation: A LastEvaluatedKey means the result set was paginated and more items exist. Pass it as ExclusiveStartKey on the next request to continue. When it is absent, you have retrieved all matching items.

questions.question: An application makes many repeated reads of the same DynamoDB items and needs microsecond latency. Which feature should be added?
questions.explanation: DAX is an in-memory cache for DynamoDB that delivers microsecond read latency for repeated reads. GSIs support alternate query patterns, Streams capture changes, and capacity settings do not add caching.

questions.question: An API Gateway REST API needs to reduce backend calls for identical GET requests. Which feature helps MOST?
questions.explanation: API Gateway caching stores responses for a configurable TTL, so identical requests are served from cache and never reach the backend. Usage plans throttle, and validation/mTLS address input and security.

questions.question: A mobile app needs to let users sign in with email/password and then call AWS APIs with temporary credentials. Which combination is appropriate?
options: Cognito User Pool for sign-in, Identity Pool for AWS credentials
IAM users for each mobile user
Access keys embedded in the app
questions.explanation: A Cognito User Pool handles user sign-in/directory; a Cognito Identity Pool exchanges that identity for temporary AWS credentials via IAM roles. IAM users per end-user and embedded keys are anti-patterns.

questions.question: An EC2 instance's memory usage is not visible in CloudWatch by default. How can you collect memory metrics?
options: Install and configure the CloudWatch agent
questions.explanation: Memory and disk usage are guest-OS metrics that EC2 does not publish by default. The CloudWatch agent (or legacy scripts) must be installed on the instance to push memory/disk metrics.

questions.question: You need SSH-like shell access to private EC2 instances with no open port 22, no bastion host, and full audit logging. Which service should you use?
options: EC2 Instance Connect over the internet
questions.explanation: SSM Session Manager provides shell access controlled by IAM, requires no inbound ports or bastion, and logs sessions to CloudWatch/S3, making it the most secure option.

questions.question: You must apply OS security patches to a fleet of EC2 instances on a schedule with compliance reporting. Which service automates this?
questions.explanation: SSM Patch Manager automates patching on a schedule via maintenance windows and reports compliance. Config tracks configuration state, Inspector finds vulnerabilities, and CloudFormation provisions infrastructure.

questions.question: A CloudWatch alarm should notify an on-call team and trigger an Auto Scaling action when CPU is high. What does the alarm send its notification action to?
options: An Amazon SNS topic (and an Auto Scaling policy)
questions.explanation: CloudWatch alarms invoke actions such as publishing to an SNS topic (which fans out to email/SMS/Lambda) and triggering Auto Scaling policies. Alarms do not email addresses directly without SNS.

questions.question: Which AWS Backup capability lets you meet a requirement to keep copies of backups in a second Region for disaster recovery?
options: Cross-Region copy in a backup plan
questions.explanation: AWS Backup plans support cross-Region copy so recovery points are replicated to another Region for DR. Vault lock enforces immutability, and lifecycle moves backups to cheaper tiers.

questions.question: Which AWS service uses machine learning to continuously analyze VPC Flow Logs, DNS logs, and CloudTrail to detect threats like crypto-mining or credential compromise?
questions.explanation: GuardDuty is the managed threat-detection service that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs. Macie classifies sensitive data in S3, Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities, and Config tracks resource compliance.

questions.question: A company must discover and classify sensitive data such as PII stored in Amazon S3. Which service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Macie uses machine learning to discover and classify sensitive data (like PII and credentials) in S3. GuardDuty is threat detection, Secrets Manager stores secrets, and KMS manages encryption keys.

questions.question: You need Layer 7 protection to block SQL injection and cross-site scripting for an application behind an Application Load Balancer. Which service should you attach?
questions.explanation: AWS WAF inspects HTTP(S) requests (Layer 7) and can block SQLi, XSS, and rate-based abuse; it attaches to ALB, CloudFront, and API Gateway. Shield handles DDoS, and SG/NACLs operate at layers 3/4.

questions.question: Across an AWS Organization, you must guarantee that no account can disable AWS CloudTrail, even by an account administrator. What enforces this?
questions.explanation: An SCP that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging/DeleteTrail sets the maximum permissions for member accounts, so even admins cannot disable CloudTrail. Permission boundaries and identity/resource policies act within a single account.

questions.question: An organization wants to prevent any member account from disabling CloudTrail, regardless of that account's IAM permissions. What should be used?
options: A Service Control Policy (SCP) in AWS Organizations
An IAM identity policy on each user
questions.explanation: SCPs set the maximum available permissions for accounts in an OU/organization. A deny SCP on cloudtrail:StopLogging prevents even account admins from disabling CloudTrail. Permission boundaries and identity policies act only within a single account.

questions.question: A company needs many VPCs across multiple accounts to communicate with each other and on-premises through a single hub, with transitive routing. Which service is the BEST fit?
questions.explanation: Transit Gateway is a hub-and-spoke router that connects many VPCs and on-premises networks with transitive routing, avoiding a full mesh of peering connections. VPC Peering is non-transitive.

questions.question: During a large migration, which of the 7 Rs describes moving an application to the cloud with minimal changes (a 'lift and shift')?
questions.explanation: Rehost is lift-and-shift: move the workload as-is (often with Application Migration Service). Replatform makes minor optimizations, Refactor re-architects, and Repurchase moves to a different product (e.g., SaaS).

questions.question: A workload must fail over to a second Region with an RPO of seconds and near-zero RTO, serving live traffic from both Regions. Which DR strategy is this?
questions.explanation: Active-active (multi-Region) serves traffic from both Regions simultaneously, giving the lowest RTO/RPO at the highest cost. Pilot light and warm standby have larger RTOs; backup/restore is the slowest.

questions.question: A pipeline must fail and stop deployment if unit tests fail before packaging the artifact. Which service runs the build and tests in a CodePipeline stage?
questions.explanation: CodeBuild compiles code, runs tests, and produces artifacts; a failing test fails the build and halts the pipeline. CodeDeploy handles deployment, CodeCommit is source control, and CodeArtifact is a package repository.

questions.question: You need zero-downtime deployments for an ECS service where a new version runs alongside the old and traffic shifts only after health checks pass. Which strategy fits?
questions.explanation: Blue/green stands up the new (green) version beside the old (blue), validates health, then shifts traffic, enabling zero-downtime and fast rollback. CodeDeploy supports blue/green for ECS and Lambda.

questions.question: Application logs from EC2 must be centralized and queried with a SQL-like language for troubleshooting. Which combination is appropriate?
options: Store logs on the instance only
CloudWatch agent to CloudWatch Logs, queried with Logs Insights
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent ships logs to CloudWatch Logs, and Logs Insights provides a query language for fast troubleshooting. CloudTrail records API activity, not application logs.

questions.question: A team wants to detect when a deployed CloudFormation stack's resources have been changed manually outside of the template. Which feature helps?
questions.explanation: Drift detection compares actual resource configuration against the stack template to find manual (out-of-band) changes. Change sets preview updates, nested stacks compose templates, and StackSets deploy across accounts/Regions.

questions.question: A company needs a dedicated, private, consistent-bandwidth connection between its data center and AWS that does not traverse the public internet. Which service should they use?
questions.explanation: Direct Connect provides a dedicated private physical connection with consistent bandwidth and lower latency than internet-based VPN. A Site-to-Site VPN runs over the public internet.

questions.question: You must capture metadata about accepted and rejected IP traffic to and from network interfaces in a VPC for security analysis. Which feature provides this?
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs record metadata (source/dest, ports, ACCEPT/REJECT) for traffic at the VPC, subnet, or ENI level. Traffic Mirroring copies full packets to an appliance; CloudTrail logs API calls.

questions.question: Two VPCs with overlapping CIDR blocks must exchange data for a specific service. VPC Peering is not possible due to the overlap. Which service can expose the service privately?
questions.explanation: PrivateLink exposes a specific service through an interface endpoint, which works even with overlapping CIDRs because it does not require routable, non-overlapping address space like peering or Transit Gateway do.

questions.question: An application needs a static IP address and ultra-low-latency Layer 4 load balancing for a TCP workload. Which load balancer should be used?
questions.explanation: The Network Load Balancer operates at Layer 4, offers ultra-low latency, and provides a static IP per AZ (and Elastic IP support). ALB is Layer 7 with changing IPs, and GLB is for inline appliances.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning trains a model on labeled input-output pairs to predict outcomes for new inputs?
questions.explanation: Supervised learning uses labeled data (inputs paired with known outputs) to learn a mapping for prediction. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data, and reinforcement learning learns from rewards.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides access to foundation models (such as Anthropic Claude and Amazon Titan) through a single API for building generative AI applications?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers foundation models from multiple providers via one API, plus features like knowledge bases and agents. SageMaker is a full ML platform; Comprehend and Rekognition are task-specific AI services.

questions.question: A company wants a generative AI chatbot to answer using their own internal documents without retraining the model. Which technique should they use?
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves relevant company documents (often from a vector store) and adds them to the prompt as context, so the model answers from private data without retraining. Fine-tuning changes model weights and is heavier.

questions.question: Which Amazon Bedrock feature helps block harmful content and restrict topics in generative AI application responses?
questions.explanation: Guardrails for Amazon Bedrock let you define denied topics and content filters to promote safe, responsible outputs. Knowledge Bases add RAG, Agents orchestrate tasks, and Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity.

questions.question: A team needs a serverless ETL service to crawl data in S3, infer schema into a catalog, and run Spark transformations. Which service fits?
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is serverless ETL with crawlers, a Data Catalog, and Spark-based jobs. Athena queries data in place with SQL, EMR runs managed big-data clusters you size, and Redshift is a data warehouse.

questions.question: Analysts want to run ad-hoc SQL queries directly against data in S3 without loading it into a database, paying only per data scanned. Which service is BEST?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena runs serverless SQL directly on S3 data and charges per data scanned, ideal for ad-hoc analysis. Reducing scanned data with partitioning and columnar formats (Parquet) lowers cost.

questions.question: A pipeline must reliably load streaming data into Amazon S3 and Redshift with minimal management and near-real-time delivery. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) is fully managed and delivers streaming data to destinations like S3, Redshift, and OpenSearch with buffering. Kinesis Data Streams requires you to manage consumers.

questions.question: To reduce Athena cost and improve performance on a large S3 dataset, which optimization is MOST effective?
options: Partition data and use a columnar format like Parquet
Increase the S3 bucket size limit
questions.explanation: Partitioning prunes the data scanned, and columnar formats like Parquet (with compression) reduce bytes read, directly lowering Athena cost and improving query speed. CSV scans far more data.

questions.question: Which SageMaker capability performs automatic hyperparameter optimization to find the best model configuration?
questions.explanation: Automatic Model Tuning runs many training jobs with different hyperparameters (Bayesian/random search) to optimize a chosen metric. Ground Truth labels data, Feature Store manages features, and Clarify detects bias.

questions.question: A model receives sporadic, unpredictable traffic and the team wants to avoid paying for idle inference infrastructure. Which SageMaker inference option is BEST?
options: Multi-model endpoint on a large instance
questions.explanation: Serverless Inference automatically scales to zero when idle and handles intermittent traffic without provisioning instances. Always-on real-time endpoints cost money while idle, and Batch Transform is for offline bulk scoring.

questions.question: After deployment, a model's accuracy degrades as incoming data distribution changes over time. Which SageMaker feature detects this drift?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Model Monitor detects data-quality and model-quality drift in production. Pipelines orchestrate MLOps, Data Wrangler prepares data, and Neo compiles models for edge/optimized runtimes.

questions.question: A generative AI application must ground responses in a company's proprietary knowledge base stored as documents. Which Bedrock capability provides managed retrieval augmentation?
questions.explanation: Bedrock Knowledge Bases provide managed RAG: ingesting documents, creating embeddings, and retrieving relevant context at query time. Guardrails enforce safety, and Provisioned Throughput reserves capacity.

questions.question: To make a foundation model call external tools or APIs and complete multi-step tasks autonomously, which Bedrock feature should be used?
questions.explanation: Bedrock Agents orchestrate multi-step tasks, calling APIs/tools and using knowledge bases to fulfill user requests. Guardrails handle safety, and prompt templates alone cannot invoke external actions.

questions.question: Lowering the 'temperature' setting when calling a foundation model generally results in what?
questions.explanation: Lower temperature reduces randomness, producing more deterministic and focused output, useful for factual tasks. Higher temperature increases diversity and creativity. Temperature does not directly set length.

questions.question: Which AWS Well-Architected Framework pillar focuses on the ability of a system to recover from failures and meet demand?
questions.explanation: The Reliability pillar covers the ability of a workload to perform its function correctly and consistently, including recovering from failures and dynamically acquiring resources to meet demand.

questions.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, which task is the customer's responsibility?
options: Configuring security groups and IAM policies
Replacing failed disks in the storage fleet
questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud, which includes configuring IAM, security groups, and encrypting their data. AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud (hardware, hypervisor, facilities).

questions.question: Which AWS pricing model offers the largest discount for a one- or three-year commitment to a consistent amount of compute usage?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans offer lower prices in exchange for a commitment to a consistent amount of usage (measured in $/hour) for a 1- or 3-year term. Spot can be cheaper per-hour but is interruptible and not a commitment discount.

questions.question: A company wants a managed service to run containers without managing the underlying EC2 instances. Which option is BEST?
questions.explanation: AWS Fargate is a serverless compute engine for containers that removes the need to provision and manage EC2 instances. It works with both ECS and EKS.

questions.question: Which tool lets you visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time?
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides an interface to visualize and analyze cost and usage data over time. CloudTrail logs API activity, Config tracks resource configuration, and Trusted Advisor gives best-practice checks.

questions.question: An application must decouple a fleet of producers from consumers and guarantee each message is processed by exactly one consumer. Which service fits BEST?
questions.explanation: Amazon SQS is a message queue where each message is consumed by a single consumer, decoupling producers from consumers. SNS is pub/sub (fan-out to many subscribers).

questions.question: How should an EC2 application obtain credentials to call AWS APIs securely?
options: Hard-code access keys in the application
Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instance
questions.explanation: Attaching an IAM role provides temporary, automatically rotated credentials via the instance metadata service. Never hard-code or embed long-term access keys.

questions.question: A read-heavy relational workload on Amazon RDS needs to scale read capacity without impacting the primary. What should you add?
questions.explanation: Read replicas offload read traffic from the primary and can scale horizontally. A Multi-AZ standby is for failover and does not serve reads. RDS Proxy pools connections but doesn't add read capacity.

questions.question: Which S3 storage class automatically moves objects between access tiers based on changing access patterns with no retrieval fees?
questions.explanation: S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves objects between frequent and infrequent access tiers based on usage, with no retrieval fees, ideal for unpredictable access patterns.

questions.question: A company needs to give a mobile app temporary, limited access to upload to S3 without distributing AWS credentials. What is the BEST approach?
options: Create an IAM user per device
Use Amazon Cognito with IAM roles for temporary credentials
Share a single access key with all users
questions.explanation: Amazon Cognito federates identities and issues temporary, scoped AWS credentials via IAM roles, avoiding distribution of long-term keys and never requiring a public bucket.

questions.question: A Lambda function needs to process items from a DynamoDB table as they change. What should you configure?
options: A CloudWatch alarm on the table
A DynamoDB Stream as an event source for Lambda
An SNS topic on the table
questions.explanation: DynamoDB Streams capture item-level changes and can trigger a Lambda function via an event source mapping, enabling change-driven processing.

questions.question: A developer wants distributed tracing across a microservices app on AWS to find latency bottlenecks. Which service helps?
questions.explanation: AWS X-Ray provides end-to-end distributed tracing, showing a service map and latency for each segment, ideal for locating bottlenecks in microservices.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to store a database password used by a Lambda function, with automatic rotation?
options: An S3 object with public read
questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager securely stores secrets and supports automatic rotation. Plaintext environment variables and hard-coded values are insecure.

questions.question: Which service can automatically remediate a noncompliant resource configuration (e.g., an open security group) when detected?
questions.explanation: AWS Config rules can detect noncompliant resources and trigger automatic remediation actions (via SSM Automation documents), such as removing an overly permissive rule.

questions.question: An operator needs to apply an OS patch across hundreds of EC2 instances on a schedule without SSH. Which service is BEST?
questions.explanation: Systems Manager Patch Manager automates patching of managed instances on a schedule using maintenance windows, with no need for SSH or bastion hosts.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to centrally govern multiple AWS accounts, apply guardrails, and consolidate billing. Which combination is BEST?
options: A single large account with many IAM users
AWS Organizations with Service Control Policies
Separate unrelated accounts with manual policies
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing and centralized governance; Service Control Policies (SCPs) enforce guardrails across member accounts.

questions.question: Which AWS service helps discover on-premises servers and their dependencies to plan a migration?
questions.explanation: AWS Application Discovery Service collects configuration and dependency data from on-premises servers to help plan migrations. DataSync/Snowball move data; Macie classifies sensitive data.

questions.question: Which deployment strategy shifts a small percentage of traffic to a new version first to limit blast radius?
questions.explanation: A canary deployment routes a small share of traffic to the new version, monitors it, then gradually shifts the rest, limiting the impact of a bad release.

questions.question: You need a single view of metrics, logs, and traces plus automated alarms for a production app. Which combination is core to this on AWS?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch centralizes metrics, logs, dashboards, and alarms, while X-Ray adds distributed tracing, together providing full observability.

questions.question: Which service uses ML and threat intelligence to continuously detect malicious activity such as unusual API calls or crypto-mining?
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat-detection service that analyzes CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs using ML to flag malicious or anomalous behavior.

questions.question: A team must ensure S3 objects are encrypted with keys they can audit and rotate, with usage logged in CloudTrail. Which option is BEST?
options: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
No encryption, rely on bucket policy
questions.explanation: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key gives control over key policies, rotation, and detailed CloudTrail logging of key usage, satisfying audit requirements.

questions.question: A company needs a private, dedicated, consistent-bandwidth connection between its data center and AWS. Which service provides this?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated private network connection with consistent bandwidth and lower latency than internet-based VPN. VPN is encrypted but rides the public internet.

questions.question: To connect hundreds of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub, which service scales BEST?
questions.explanation: AWS Transit Gateway acts as a central hub connecting many VPCs and on-premises networks, avoiding the O(n^2) complexity of a full VPC peering mesh.

questions.question: Which term describes providing a few examples within a prompt to guide a foundation model's response?
questions.explanation: Few-shot prompting includes a small number of examples in the prompt to steer the model's output without changing its weights. Fine-tuning and pre-training modify the model itself.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides access to multiple foundation models through a single API for building generative AI applications?
questions.explanation: Amazon Bedrock offers access to foundation models from multiple providers via a single API, with features like knowledge bases and agents for building GenAI apps.

questions.question: Which practice helps reduce harmful or biased outputs from a generative AI application?
questions.explanation: Guardrails and content filtering (e.g., Amazon Bedrock Guardrails) help block harmful, biased, or off-topic content, supporting responsible AI. Human oversight remains important.

questions.question: A model performs well on training data but poorly on new data. What is this called and one common fix?
options: Overfitting; apply regularization or more data
questions.explanation: High training accuracy but poor generalization indicates overfitting. Common fixes include regularization, dropout, gathering more/representative data, or simplifying the model.

questions.question: Which Amazon SageMaker feature hosts a model for low-latency, real-time inference behind an HTTPS endpoint?
questions.explanation: SageMaker Real-Time (hosted) Endpoints serve low-latency, synchronous inference over HTTPS. Batch Transform is for offline bulk inference.

questions.question: Which service is a serverless, fully managed extract-transform-load (ETL) service that can catalog data and run Spark jobs?
questions.explanation: AWS Glue is a serverless ETL service with a data catalog and managed Apache Spark jobs. Athena queries data in place with SQL; Redshift is a data warehouse.

questions.question: To run interactive SQL queries directly against data stored in Amazon S3 without loading it first, which service is BEST?
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena is a serverless, interactive query service that runs standard SQL directly against data in Amazon S3, with no infrastructure to manage.

questions.question: Which technique augments a foundation model's responses with an organization's own documents at query time, without retraining?
questions.explanation: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant documents (e.g., from a vector store or knowledge base) and adds them to the prompt, grounding responses without retraining.

questions.question: What does a vector embedding represent in a generative AI/RAG system?
options: A numeric representation of text capturing semantic meaning
questions.explanation: Embeddings are numeric vectors that capture the semantic meaning of text (or other data), enabling similarity search that powers retrieval in RAG systems.
